# Unattended build controller

The controller runs on Render-1 as Patrick's systemd user timer, togavsu-build-controller.timer. It starts after boot and runs again two minutes after each completed tick. Linger is enabled, so neither an open chat nor a logged-in desktop is required. Builds, tests and application installs remain in Cursor cloud VMs and GitHub-hosted CI; Render-1 runs only control operations.

## Automatic cycle
- Adopt the four existing Cursor agents and their two already-used correction rounds.
- Wait while an agent or CI is active.
- Read the independent Codex artifact from the GitHub Actions check for that exact PR head and current main. Reject another PR's artifact, a stale base/head, malformed data or a spoofed non-Actions check.
- Send failures back to the same Cursor agent and PR, with regression tests and replacement of stale original PR evidence required. Persist the delivery intent before submission. A lost response requires the integration lead to verify delivery before reconciling the persisted intent; a different latest run ID alone is not proof, and it is never blindly resubmitted.
- Refresh branches against main. Conflicts go back to the owning worker; successful refreshes trigger fresh tests/review. No forced updates or protection bypasses.
- Merge only after every reported Actions check succeeds, all named required jobs exist, the exact-revision Codex report passes with no findings, and main/PR head still match. Verify that branch protection still requires PRs, strict checks and enforcement for admins. GitHub makes the final protected merge decision.
- Record the protected merge as a bounded dependency. Launch ready assignments automatically, with at most four occupied implementation slots and a durable UUID per new agent.
- Cloud integration assignments compose the separate packages into the actual running product and must provide real product CI and passing integration reports. The final release remains subject to all 52 criteria; merged scaffolding is never full product acceptance.

The controller and integration lead own GitHub CI monitoring, review feedback and future dispatch. Every launch and follow-up prompt forbids worker-created background CI subscriptions (including `github:ci:branch`), CI-wait continuation events and asynchronous background waits. Workers may make read-only synchronous checks, then return the exact pushed SHA, local test commands/results and pending CI links, and finish the run. Pending CI is reported honestly and followed by the controller. This prompt boundary does not cancel existing subscriptions or replace the exact-run, capacity, review or uncertain-delivery guards.

## Limits and recovery
The controller allows three correction attempts for each individual finding or check failure in an assignment. The lifetime `repair_count` remains an audit total and is not a stop by itself. `max_repairs` in the existing pinned plan now sets the per-problem limit; the plan needs no migration.

Problem identity comes from sorted Codex finding files/details with numeric line-location suffixes, inline references to the finding file, and explicit line references normalized, failed CI job names, missing CI job names, or the integration-evidence error. Review summaries, priorities, ordering, base/head SHAs, check URLs, PR body edits and Cursor run IDs don't reset that budget. Interrupted runs, missing PRs and persistent drafts each have their own stable problem identity, and their budgets count consecutive repeats only. A finished run resets the interruption count, a discovered PR resets the missing-PR count, a ready PR resets the draft count, and a new PR head or a verified merge resets all three, so three interruptions weeks apart with progress between them never exhaust the budget. Counts stay in `repair_problems`, including when problems alternate or companion findings change. A correction for [A, B] spends one attempt on A and one on B; a later report of [A, C] keeps A's count and backoff. Duplicate findings in one report spend only one attempt. Reworded findings can form a new identity; this is deterministic duplicate detection, not a claim that the code improved. The per-assignment `correction_volume` covers that gap: it counts corrections dispatched under this policy and only a verified merge ends it. At `correction_attention_threshold` corrections (default 10) the task reports `stalled.kind=high_correction_volume` and `health=needs_attention` while corrections continue. At `max_corrections_per_assignment` corrections (default 30) further corrections are held with `stalled.kind=correction_ceiling` for the integration lead; observation, CI and review continue, and a passing exact-revision review still merges.

After a completed correction leaves the same problem, the controller waits five minutes before a second attempt and ten minutes before a third, measured from dispatch. Each recovery asks the same worker to diagnose why its prior approach failed. It requires an observed terminal run, preserves the original delivery history, persists a fresh intent before POST, and shares the four-worker limit. A lost response never triggers an automatic replay or an acknowledgement inferred from a changed latest run ID. Its durable intent reserves a slot and reports an actionable safety halt until the integration lead independently verifies delivery. An acknowledged run reserves a worker slot and blocks PR actions, including a green merge, until its exact saved run ID is observed. Before that exact run is seen, an older stale run, any unrelated run and a missing ID cannot release that reservation. If Cursor's latest run is already a different ID, the controller fetches the acknowledged run by ID and counts it as seen when the response matches its ID, its agent and a known status; a run that was reported as latest before that check is newer only if Cursor's `createdAt` times show it. A 404, mismatch or error keeps the slot and the PR block and is recorded as the task's `last_error`. Once it is seen, the controller saves `last_dispatched_run_observed`; a later identified run that is neither the predecessor nor a run reported before it is treated as a newer run, so a continuation counts as an active worker and a finished one allows PR processing, while the predecessor, those earlier runs and missing IDs still hold the slot. Each new acknowledgement clears that record. Its visibility is checked before active-worker and pending-CI handling. If it still isn't visible after fifteen minutes, it is reported as stalled; seeing the exact acknowledged run clears only that visibility warning. Base-controller records have no predecessor ID or dispatch time. Until Cursor reports their saved acknowledged run ID, or the same by-ID fetch confirms it, they conservatively reserve a slot and block PR actions. Their fifteen-minute inspection clock starts at the first uncertain observation after upgrade, without inventing a past dispatch time.

If any current finding or check reaches its per-problem limit, the whole correction is held and the assignment reports `stalled.kind=no_progress` with an instruction for the integration lead to inspect its existing agent and PR. Observation continues, so genuinely different findings can proceed without manually clearing state; independent tasks also continue. The integration lead handles routine diagnosis within the approved assignment. Don't delete state, reset counters to make the status look healthy, or relaunch a worker whose delivery outcome is unknown.

The exact obsolete halt `Three correction cycles exhausted; independent work may continue` is automatically archived in `recovered_halts` and cleared. No other old halt is automatically cleared by this migration. An unrelated safety halt also survives observation of a predecessor run followed by reconciliation of an uncertain delivery. Routine Git conflict resolution retains its separate three-attempt bound. An unavailable review still gets one infrastructure rerun per base/head. Ownership, protected-file, review, branch-protection, acceptance and ambiguous-delivery gates stay fail-closed.

A failed control request is recorded and retried by later observation, not by bypassing checks. Every failed observation of a submitted worker retains its capacity slot. A latest-run HTTP 404 is an unavailable observation, not proof that the agent was deleted. Only a 404 from the agent endpoint permits retrying an unconfirmed initial create, using its original durable ID, and only when no acknowledged run or delivery intent is outstanding. Existing workers and outstanding deliveries remain reserved for inspection; observation errors never overwrite unrelated safety halts. External service failures may prevent progress. Status is persisted in .build-state/status.json and a dedicated comment on GitHub build issue #1 is updated when task state changes.

Observation validation uses the [documented Cursor v1 run statuses](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints): active `CREATING`, `RUNNING`, `WAITING_FOR_BACKGROUND_WORK`; terminal `FINISHED`, `ERROR`, `CANCELLED`, `EXPIRED`. Only an identified terminal run can release capacity or allow correction/PR processing. Missing, unknown or malformed statuses, malformed identities and terminal snapshots without an ID retain the slot and report a transient observation error, including during adoption and initial-launch reconciliation. The fetched run must match the requested agent and latest run ID; agent lifecycle data cannot substitute for a run result. Agent `ACTIVE` without an available run is only a conservative busy signal. Valid later observations clear the transient error automatically while preserving unrelated holds and delivery intents.

## Freeze and recovery
Immediate freeze: stop both togavsu-build-controller.timer and togavsu-build-controller.service through systemctl --user. Create .build-state/STOP to keep it paused across a later timer start. A STOP file is checked at the beginning of each tick.

State lives in the control checkout's ignored .build-state directory: controller.json contains durable IDs, delivery/merge intents, correction budgets and results; agents.json preserves the original launches. Investigate a stopped item and reconcile its external run, PR and independent evidence before the authorized integration lead makes a targeted recovery. Routine supervision doesn't wait for Patrick. Recovery can't waive review, CI, ownership, protection or product acceptance.

An outstanding delivery intent (a lost POST response) is reconciled without editing controller.json. Stop the timer, confirm the run in Cursor, then run `python3 /home/patrick/.local/share/togavsu-controller/run_controller.py --plan /home/patrick/.local/share/togavsu-controller/controller-plan.json --state /mnt/claude-workspace/nolan-pms/togavsu/.build-state --reconcile-intent TASK RUN_ID --operator NAME` and restart the timer. It fetches that run by ID, requires its ID and agent to match, refuses the intent's predecessor and the previous acknowledged run, and refuses a run whose `createdAt` is earlier than the intent. When Cursor gives no `createdAt`, only the ID and agent are checked, and the audit entry says so. On success it acknowledges the intent with that run, clears only the uncertain-delivery halts, appends an entry with the operator name to the task's `reconciled` list and the event log, and sends no prompt. It runs no tick; `--dry-run` prints the change without saving it.

## Health and supervision

`status.json` is written on every non-paused tick, including a merge tick and a failed top-level control request. `updated` is the last status publication time, not evidence of product progress. The issue #1 status comment changes only when its substantive state changes. A monitor should read the local status as well as the issue because GitHub itself can be unavailable. If comment POST/PATCH fails, a separate local-only write records `publication_error` and `health=needs_attention`; that path never retries the remote mutation recursively. A later successful publication clears its error without clearing current task or observation errors.

- `health` is `needs_attention` if any unfinished assignment is halted, stalled, at or above the correction attention threshold, has a control error or has an unresolved launch/delivery outcome. Otherwise it is `observing`; that doesn't assert product acceptance.
- `tick_error` records a top-level observation failure. Task `last_error` records an assignment control failure. `last_successful_tick` in controller.json is only a successful control heartbeat and advances only after status publication succeeds.
- `last_productive_progress` is null until a protected merge is verified under this policy. It then gives `time`, `task` and `merge_sha`. A bounded merge doesn't complete a phase or release.
- Each task's `last_submission` gives `head` and `observed_at`. A new candidate is not accepted progress. `repair_window` gives the most-consumed current problem fingerprint, attempts and, after dispatch, `last_dispatch_at`. Dispatch waits for the latest backoff deadline among every current problem, and its persisted intent names all budgets to increment once on acknowledgement. Lifetime `repair_count` remains visible.
- `active_watch` gives the last confirmed `run_id` (or null), the current `observed_run_id` (null when unavailable), and the time continuous activity was first observed. Missing IDs preserve that deadline and warning. Binding an initially unknown ID does not prove a new run started; only a different confirmed ID resets the watch. At thirty minutes the task reports `stalled.kind=active_run`, including that run ID and start time. Changing status/heartbeat timestamps doesn't extend the deadline. The optional plan field `active_run_timeout_seconds` overrides the default 1800 seconds. This is an inspection deadline, not proof the worker failed: it never cancels or replaces the run. A finished run or a different confirmed run clears only that active-run warning. Active-watch updates never replace an unrelated warning.
- `stalled.kind=run_observation` means an acknowledged run wasn't visible after fifteen minutes. `stalled.kind=no_progress` means repeated-problem recovery is exhausted. `high_correction_volume` and `correction_ceiling` report the per-assignment correction volume. Each includes a concrete `reason`. `halted` remains a safety stop and carries its reason.

Monitor `health=needs_attention` promptly. Investigate a status older than ten minutes while the two-minute timer is enabled, and check STOP/service state before considering recovery. A read-only supervisor may inspect the existing run, PR and checks; it must reconcile uncertainty before any new dispatch. Successful timer exits never justify reporting that the product is advancing.

## Deployment and credentials
The running controller and plan are copied from a reviewed commit into /home/patrick/.local/share/togavsu-controller. They are pinned; a worker changing main cannot replace the running controller. The installed receipt records the source commit and file hashes.

The entrypoint reads only the existing CURSOR_API_KEY from Patrick's local credential file. GitHub uses the existing authenticated gh configuration. No key values are in the repository or unit files, and no control credentials are injected into build VMs. The Codex checkpoint runs Opus on the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN repository secret, billed to the Max subscription.

The deterministic controller tests cover feedback dispatch/deduplication, crash/restart durability, repeated and alternating problems, bounded backoff, legacy-cap recovery, active-run deadlines, health publication, ambiguous requests, branch conflicts, stale or forged reviews, required CI, merge races, protection rejection, dependency launches and pause behavior. A live dry-run against existing PRs precedes deployment. Run control-only validation with `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`, `python3 scripts/check_setup.py` and `git diff --check`. No product build or install belongs on Render-1.

Integration evidence is bound to a tested 40-character code revision; only report-file commits may follow that revision. Reports must exhaustively partition assigned acceptance IDs and pass every named phase case with its test command and mapped criteria. Final release permits no pending criterion. Integration leads are serialized through the dependency graph to preserve shared-file ownership. Correction dispatch and new launches share the same pre-observed four-worker capacity limit.

Each PR is bound to the Cursor agent's pinned branch and a unique task label. The independent review repeats that task ID; another assignment's PR or report cannot unlock dependencies. PR-body edits and task labels trigger fresh reviews so current validation evidence is used.

A cancelled Codex workflow is treated as superseded: the controller waits for the newer review event instead of replaying the cancelled event, which would cancel its replacement and reuse obsolete PR evidence. The existing 90-minute fresh-review deadline still applies. Non-cancelled malformed or unavailable review artifacts retain their single infrastructure retry.

## Claude Code lane backend
Setting `"worker_backend": "claude-actions"` in the controller plan replaces Cursor agents with Claude Code runs in GitHub Actions, billed to the Max subscription through the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret. Every controller gate (review, CI, merge, capacity, deadlines) is unchanged; only the worker transport differs.

The controller dispatches `.github/workflows/lane-agent.yml` on main with the agent ID, run ID, task, pinned branch, base revision and a compressed prompt. Only Patrick's account may dispatch it. The job runs with a read-only token and cannot push. Claude commits on a local branch; the job secret-scans the result and uploads a git bundle plus `lane-result.json` as the `lane-<run_id>` artifact.

When the run completes, the controller (Patrick's gh credentials on Render-1) downloads the artifact, checks that it belongs to that agent, run, task, branch and base, verifies the bundle, confirms the new head descends from the base and pushes without force. A moved branch or mismatched result is rejected, never overwritten. It then opens the PR once or updates its body. Follow-up instructions dispatch a new run from the current branch head with the original assignment attached. Dry runs never publish. Before pushing, the controller rejects a result whose commits touch a protected control-plane file or deploy/controller/, add a symlink or submodule, or change a .github/ file the assignment does not own. An owned workflow file must set top-level permissions and must not name secrets, write scopes or privileged triggers, because pushing with owner credentials runs the branch's workflows with repository secrets.

Agent records live in `.build-state/lane-agents.json`. Agents launched on Cursor before the switch keep using the Cursor API until they finish, so the entrypoint still loads CURSOR_API_KEY when it is present; it is not required. Before verifying a bundle the controller fetches its base from GitHub, because that base is often a squash merge this checkout never saw. The lane job scans every published commit, not just the net diff, and the Claude step has its own time limit below the job's so committed work is always packaged.

Tasks listed in the plan's `held_tasks` never launch, even when their dependencies are merged. Calendar and files are held until Patrick approves them; releasing a hold is a reviewed plan change.
